name: US Subscription Auto-Renewal Requirements
description: Requirements of US federal, state, DC and New York City automatic-renewal and negative-option laws for subscription businesses: disclosure, consent, acknowledgment, notice windows, cancellation and records, with citations, effective dates and enforcement. Drafted from primary sources; pending attorney review; not legal advice.
attribution: Checkbox, US Subscription Auto-Renewal Requirements Dataset, version 2026.11.01.1, https://checkbox.site/laws/data (CC BY 4.0)
disclaimer: Research data, not legal advice. Every requirement is drafted from the cited source and is pending attorney review.

laws.statute: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act (ROSCA)
laws.summary: Online negative-option sales: clear and conspicuous disclosure of all material terms before obtaining billing information, express informed consent before charging, and simple mechanisms to stop recurring charges. No amendments.
laws.scope: Applies to goods or services sold in a transaction effected on the Internet through a "negative option feature" (16 C.F.R. § 310.2(w): a provision under which the customer's silence or failure to take affirmative action to reject goods or services or to cancel the agreement is interpreted as acceptance) — i.e. free-to-pay conversions, automatic renewals and continuity plans sold online. Enforced by the FTC (violations are treated as rule violations under FTC Act § 18, enabling civil penalties and consumer redress) and by state attorneys general.

laws.statute: Electronic Fund Transfer Act / Regulation E — preauthorized transfers
laws.summary: Recurring debits from consumer asset accounts need a signed or similarly authenticated written authorization, a copy to the consumer, and 10 days' advance notice of varying amounts.
laws.scope: Debit card, prepaid card and ACH billing only (not credit cards).

laws.statute: FTC Negative Option Rule ("Use of Prenotification Negative Option Plans")
laws.summary: NOT CATALOGED. The 2024 click-to-cancel amendments (89 FR 90476) were vacated by the Eighth Circuit on July 8, 2025 (Custom Commc'ns, Inc. v. FTC, 142 F.4th 1060) and never took effect. The FTC restored the 1973 prenotification-plan rule effective Feb. 12, 2026 (91 FR 6507); it applies only to prenotification negative option plans (periodic announcements of selections), not ordinary subscriptions. An ANPRM was published Mar. 13, 2026 (91 FR 12318; comments closed Apr. 13, 2026); no proposed or final rule as of 2026-10-29. Re-check the Federal Register before relying on this.

amendments.citation: 89 FR 90476 (Nov. 15, 2024) — "Rule Concerning Recurring Subscriptions and Other Negative Option Programs"
amendments.summary: Click-to-cancel amendments; compliance date for most provisions was July 14, 2025. Vacated July 8, 2025 before taking effect.
Conforming final rule recodifying the pre-2024 prenotification rule after the vacatur.
Advance notice of proposed rulemaking (no rule text; no legal effect).

enforcement.remedies: ROSCA: FTC and state attorneys general only. Violations are treated as FTC rule violations: civil penalties up to $53,088 per violation (counted per consumer) and consumer redress (e.g. Amazon $2.5B, Adobe $150M).

laws.statute: Alaska free trial period law
laws.summary: Free trials: clear and conspicuous disclosure of all material terms, express verifiable consent, cancellation at any time during the trial and a 30-day post-trial return/refund right. No general automatic-renewal statute.

enforcement.remedies: Unfair trade practice under AS 45.50.471(b)(47); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

laws.statute: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
laws.summary: California-style law: offer terms next to consent; consent and express consent; 3-year consent records; acknowledgment; trial (> 31 days, 3-21 days) and 1-year-term (15-45 days) notices; online at-will cancellation; save-offer and same-medium rules; 7-30 day fee-change notice; annual reminder. Enforced under the Deceptive Trade Practices Act.
laws.scope: Consumers located in Arkansas (personal, family or household purposes). Exempt: persons under the Bank, Securities or Insurance Commissioners (incl. service contracts), PSC- or FCC-regulated persons (except satellite digital radio), municipal utilities, franchised service providers, and private security agencies.

enforcement.remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

laws.statute: California Automatic Renewal Law
laws.summary: Clear and conspicuous offer terms next to the consent request; affirmative (and since July 2025, express affirmative) consent; retainable acknowledgment; online "click to cancel" for online sign-ups; trial (> 31 days, 3-21 days) and 1-year-term (15-45 days) notices; 7-30 day fee-change notice; annual reminder; same-medium cancellation; limits on save offers; consent records kept 3 years. Remedies: civil (UCL) remedies only (§ 17604); unconsented goods are gifts (§ 17603).
laws.scope: Consumers (personal, family or household purposes) in California. Exempt (§ 17605): CPUC/FCC/FERC-regulated or franchised services, Department of Insurance-regulated entities, alarm company operators, banks and other licensed financial institutions, and BEAR-regulated service contract sellers.

amendments.summary: Free-trial disclosures and acknowledgment; online cancellation for online sign-ups.
Trial/promo and 1-year-term notices; at-will online termination via prominent link/button or termination email.

Express affirmative consent, consent records, misrepresentation, expanded notice contents, same-medium cancellation, phone/voicemail rules, save-offer rules, 7-30 day fee-change notice, annual reminder (contracts entered, amended or extended on or after July 1, 2025).

enforcement.remedies: No private right in the ARL itself (Mayron v. Google, 2020): plaintiffs sue under the UCL, FAL and CLRA and must show economic injury; CLRA requires a 30-day demand letter before damages. Goods or services provided without the required consent are an unconditional gift (§ 17603); all civil remedies are available (§ 17604, with a good-faith-compliance safe harbor). Public enforcement by the district attorneys' task force (CART): penalties plus restitution (HelloFresh $7.5M). Typical class settlements $0.6M-$7.5M.

laws.statute: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
laws.summary: Offer terms before execution (renewal terms capped at one year absent express written consent); adjacent, labelled links; written acknowledgment; one-step online cancellation; save-offer rule; material-change notice; renewal notice 25-40 days before renewal (yearly for sub-annual plans). Enforced exclusively by the AG and district attorneys.
laws.scope: From Feb. 16, 2026 "consumer" means any person seeking or acquiring goods or services (business purchasers included); before that, individuals buying for personal, family or household purposes. Exempt: franchised/PUC-, FCC- or FERC-regulated services, insurance-regulated entities, banks, credit unions and other licensed financial institutions, air carriers.

amendments.summary: One-step online cancellation link; online save-offer rule; AG rulemaking.
"Consumer" broadened to any person (covers business-to-business subscriptions).

enforcement.remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

laws.statute: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
laws.summary: Clear and conspicuous renewal disclosures; trial-price disclosure; affirmative consent (with a lawful consent record); trial/promo notices; material-change disclosure; online cancellation without offline steps; from July 1, 2026 annual reminders, link/button/email/phone cancellation for all agreements, phone and voicemail rules, CUTPA liability.
laws.scope: Connecticut-resident consumers; agreements entered into or amended on or after Oct. 1, 2023. Excluded: franchised or PURA/FCC/FERC-regulated services, insurance-regulated entities, banks and credit unions, and any global or national service largely or predominantly consisting of audiovisual content (video streaming).

amendments.summary: "Clearly and conspicuously disclose" definition; lawful consent-record consideration.
Annual reminder; cancellation channels for all agreements; phone/voicemail and save-offer rules; CUTPA enforcement.

enforcement.remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

laws.statute: Delaware consumer contracts — automatic renewal provisions
laws.summary: Clear and conspicuous disclosure of automatic renewal terms; 30-60 day notice before each extension past the first 12 months (renewals of more than one month); easy cancellation for all auto-renewing contracts and online cancellation for online contracts. Treble damages; renewals in violation are voidable; 30-day notice-and-cure before consumer suits.
laws.scope: Consumers buying or leasing merchandise (goods, intangibles, real estate or services, other than insurance) primarily for personal, family or household purposes; contracts up to $50,000. Exempt: PSC, Insurance Commission and FCC matters, residential leases, banking organizations.

amendments.summary: Technical corrections only (no substantive change).

enforcement.remedies: Private suit with treble damages; renewals in violation are voidable; 30-day notice-and-cure before consumer suits.

laws.statute: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
laws.summary: Renewal provision and cancellation procedure disclosed clearly, conspicuously and next to the consent request; post-trial price; 30-60 day renewal notices for 12-month+ terms (first renewal and yearly); 15-30 day trial notice and separate renewal consent for trials of a month or more. Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (good-faith-error defense).
laws.scope: "Consumer" is any person acquiring goods or services (no personal-use limitation). Exempt: DISB-regulated insurers, banks and other depository institutions, PSC/FCC/FERC-regulated services, and service contracts (§ 28A-204).

enforcement.remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

laws.statute: Florida automatic renewal of service contracts
laws.summary: Service contracts with automatic renewal provisions: clear and conspicuous disclosure; 30-60 day notice before the cancellation deadline for 12-month+ contracts renewing for more than a month; cancellation by the same means as acceptance. Violations void the renewal provision.
laws.scope: Service contracts only. Exempt: financial and depository institutions (and affiliates), health studios, entities licensed under chs. 624, 627, 634, 636 or 641, electric utilities, and certain ch. 180 private utility companies.

amendments.summary: Same-manner, same-means cancellation.

enforcement.remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

laws.statute: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
laws.summary: Online subscriptions with terms over 31 days: offer terms next to consent; consent before charging; acknowledgment; notice before or within three days after charging; online cancellation; material-change notice. AG enforcement only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.
laws.scope: Natural persons residing in Georgia, personal/family/household purposes; online offers only. Exempt: franchised or PSC/Agriculture/FCC/FERC-regulated services, insurance-regulated entities, financial institutions and bank holding companies, foreign banks.

enforcement.remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

laws.statute: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
laws.summary: Disclosure of renewal/continuous-service clauses and cancellation procedure; affirmative consent; retainable acknowledgment; 30-60 day notice for 12-month+ contracts; cancellation channel; material-change notice; knowing violations or failure to cancel on request are UDAP violations (§ 480-2).
laws.scope: Consumers as defined in § 480-1. Exempt: chapter 412 financial institutions, chapter 431/432/432D insurers, chapter 269 telecommunications providers, and cable operators (ch. 440G/FCC-regulated activities).

amendments.summary: Continuous service, consent, acknowledgment, cancellation mechanism, material change, failure-to-cancel liability.
Cable-operator exemption updated (no substantive change for subscriptions).

enforcement.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

laws.statute: Idaho cancellation of subscriptions law
laws.summary: Online subscriptions: clear and conspicuous renewal terms and cancellation methods; online cancellation mechanism with no fee; toll-free, prominently displayed phone number if a phone option exists; 30-60 day notice for renewals of 12 months or more.
laws.scope: Internet subscriptions with Idaho consumers. Exempt: franchised or PUC/FCC/FERC-regulated services; insurers and their affiliates (including § 41-6203 service products).

amendments.summary: Removed the two-cancellation-methods notice requirement.

enforcement.remedies: Idaho Consumer Protection Act violation: Attorney General enforcement, no private right of action; good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

laws.statute: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
laws.summary: Offer terms next to consent; consent before charging; acknowledgment; trial/promo notice (15+ days, at least 3 days before the deadline); 30-60 day written notice for 12-month+ contracts; online cancellation for online sign-ups. Violations are Consumer Fraud Act violations (good-faith-error defense with refund).
laws.scope: Consumer contracts (not business-to-business). Exempt: banks and other financial institutions, utilities under Art. XXII of the Public Utilities Act, Department of Insurance-regulated parties, and contracts extended because the consumer changed the terms.

amendments.summary: Cancellation mechanism and online cancellation for online offers.
Offer terms, consent, acknowledgment; B2B exclusion.
Notice during free trials/promotional periods of 15 days or more.

enforcement.remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

laws.statute: Kentucky automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
laws.summary: Offer terms next to consent; affirmative consent; acknowledgment; cancellation mechanism; online cancellation for online sign-ups; material-change notice. AG enforcement (injunction, restitution, up to $500 per violation) after a first-violation cure with prorated refund; no renewal or trial reminder duties.
laws.scope: Individuals buying for personal, family or household purposes; contracts entered into from Jan. 1, 2024. Exempt (§ 365.404): franchised/PSC/FCC/FERC-regulated services, insurers and service-contract providers, banks, credit unions, savings associations, consumer loan companies, in-vehicle/roadside/travel subscription services, solid waste services.

enforcement.remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution, up to $500 per violation) after a first-violation cure with prorated refund.

laws.statute: Louisiana contracts with automatic renewal clauses
laws.summary: Clear and conspicuous disclosure of the automatic renewal clause and of how to cancel. Contracts renewed in violation revert to thirty-day renewals; good-faith-error defense with refund.
laws.scope: Consumer contracts entered into from Jan. 1, 2011; contracts cancellable on one month's written notice after the initial period are exempt.

laws.statute: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
laws.summary: Effective Jan. 1, 2027: offer terms next to acceptance (renewal terms capped at one year absent express written consent); affirmative consent; acknowledgment; one-year consent records; pre-billing notice; easy cancellation; material-change notice; notice at least 3 days before renewals of 12+ months, material changes and trial conversions. AG civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.
laws.scope: Consumers buying for personal, family or household purposes. Excludes persons with fewer than 50 employees or under $5 million annual revenue (with affiliates), rental-purchase agreements, financial institutions, insurers, FCC-regulated services, member/trade-association programs and professional subscription services; does not supersede R.S. 51:3144-3145.

enforcement.remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

laws.statute: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
laws.summary: Covered digital subscriptions (and, from 2026, health clubs). From Jan. 1, 2026: clear and easily accessible disclosure of material terms and cancellation methods; express consent by check box or other affirmative act; cancellation by the same method and manner as sign-up; notice no more than 30 days before 12-month+ renewals; treble refunds for unauthorized charges. 2020-2025: disclosure of cancellation methods, online cancellation, and 30-60 day notice before the cancellation deadline for 12-month+ subscriptions.
laws.scope: Covers only these subscriptions: online magazines, journals and periodicals; online media players; mobile apps; social networking services; internet game services; online software; and (from 2026) health club memberships (§ 1210-C(1)(A)). Physical-goods subscriptions are outside § 1210-C. Unauthorized charges must be refunded or credited at three times the amount (§ 1210-D).

amendments.summary: Express consent, same-method cancellation, misrepresentation, revised notice timing, health clubs, treble refunds, AG enforcement.

laws.statute: Maine charges after free trial period
laws.summary: Free offers that convert to paid: billing information must come directly from the consumer and the offer terms must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously. Violations are UTPA violations (§ 1210-A).

enforcement.remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

laws.statute: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
laws.summary: Renewal terms next to consent; easily accessible cancellation methods; post-trial price; consent to auto-charging for terms over one month; cancellation at least as easy as sign-up in the same medium (prominent link/button or email, no required agent); notices 3-21 days before trials over 14 days convert and 15-45 days before 1-year terms renew. Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Title 13); no private right of action under this section.
laws.scope: Exempt: businesses whose renewal practices are regulated by the Maryland Insurance Administration, entities regulated under the Service Contracts and Consumer Products Guaranty Act, and PSC-, FCC- or FERC-regulated services.

enforcement.remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

laws.statute: Massachusetts Attorney General regulation — Unfair and Deceptive Fees (recurring fees and trial offers)
laws.summary: Regulation (not a statute): written trial-offer and negative-option disclosures (including calendar cancel-by and charge dates); simple cancellation at least as easy as sign-up through the same medium that immediately stops charges; 5-30 day pre-deadline notices for periods over 31 days; per-charge or pre-deadline notices for plans of 31 days or less.
laws.scope: Applies to advertising, marketing, solicitation or offers of sale targeted to or resulting in a sale in Massachusetts; violations are unfair and deceptive practices under M.G.L. c. 93A, § 2 (private actions with multiple damages available under c. 93A).

enforcement.remedies: Unfair and deceptive practice under M.G.L. c. 93A: private actions for double or treble damages and attorney's fees (after a 30-day demand letter); AG enforcement.

laws.statute: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
laws.summary: Offer terms before acceptance; no charge before authorization; confirmation with termination options; material-change notice; 5-30 day notice for trials over 30 days; yearly notice for continuous service; no retention offers without opt-in; website termination election for sellers with account management; termination effective within 31 days. Good-faith compliance bars civil penalties (§ 325G.63).
laws.scope: Indefinite subscription agreements with Minnesota consumers (including health club, buying club and social referral contracts). Exempt (§ 325G.62): contracts governed by another automatic-renewal statute or regulation, insurance licensees, licensed technology system contractors, PUC/FCC/FERC-regulated services, FINRA/SEC/state-securities registrants.

enforcement.remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

laws.statute: New Mexico rule — Automatic Renewal of Service Contracts
laws.summary: Attorney General rule for consumer service contracts with automatic renewal provisions: 10-point clear and conspicuous renewal provision; written notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline by certified mail or monthly statement; at least 30 days to cancel after the notice; honor cancellation by any reliable means; no termination cost.
laws.scope: Regulation limited to consumer "service contracts" (any contract for service, maintenance or repair) whose automatic renewal provision keeps the contract in effect more than two months after the original term ends. Application to digital subscriptions is uncertain, so severities are one level below the catalog default. Modelled for renewal terms of three months or more.

enforcement.remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

laws.statute: New York Automatic Renewal Law (Prohibited Service Offer Practices)
laws.summary: Material terms disclosed before consent or billing information; affirmative consent; consent or a refund right for price increases; prompt retainable post-consent notice; cancellation as easy as sign-up, in the same medium and every consent medium; no obstruction; 15-45 day renewal notice (1-year terms renewing for 6+ months); 5 business day-30 day material-change notice; 3-21 day trial notice (trials over a month). AG enforcement; civil penalties $100-$1,000.
laws.scope: Consumers (personal, family or household purposes; definitions in § 527). Exempt (§ 527-a(4)): services under a municipal franchise, DFS-regulated entities, security alarm operators, banks/credit unions/financial institutions, and service contract sellers and administrators (Ins. Law § 7902). Related but not cataloged: GBL § 5-903 (renewal notice for service, maintenance or repair contracts for real or personal property). New York City consumers are also covered by the stricter DCWP "Click to Cancel" rule (US-NY.NYC.*, effective Oct. 1, 2026).

amendments.summary: 15-45 day renewal notice for initial paid terms of one year or longer.
Comprehensive rewrite of § 527-a (see file header).

enforcement.remedies: Attorney General enforcement: civil penalties of $100-$1,000 per violation (secondary figure) and restitution (1-800-Flowers $375K plus nationwide restitution; Equinox $600K). Private plaintiffs plead GBL § 349; no authority found on whether a § 527-a breach alone suffices. Goods sent without affirmative consent are an unconditional gift (§ 527-a(2)).

laws.statute: North Carolina contracts with automatic renewal clauses
laws.summary: Clear and conspicuous disclosure of the renewal clause and how to cancel; written notice 15-45 days before renewals exceeding 60 days; changed terms in 12-point bold in the notice. Violations void the renewal clause.
laws.scope: Consumer contracts for products or services. Exempt: insurers, banks and other depository institutions (and affiliates), FCC- or NC Utilities Commission-regulated entities, franchised businesses, and licensed real estate professionals.

amendments.summary: Rewrote § 75-41; added the 15-45 day notice and bold changed-terms disclosure.
Exemption for licensed real estate professionals.

enforcement.remedies: The automatic renewal clause is void and unenforceable (§ 75-41(e)); good-faith-error defense with full refund; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

laws.statute: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
laws.summary: Renewals of more than one month: clear and conspicuous terms near the offer; affirmative consent; acknowledgment; simple cancellation procedure; 30-60 day notice for renewals over six months; material-change notice; renewal periods capped at 12 months. Non-compliant provisions are void; AG and private enforcement.
laws.scope: Exempt: insurance (title 26.1), regulated public utilities and FCC-regulated services, banks, credit unions, trust companies and other title 6 financial institutions.

amendments.summary: Extended the chapter from merchandise to services; clarified definitions and remedies.

enforcement.remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

laws.summary: Consumer service contracts renewing for more than one month and lasting more than six months: 30-60 day pre-deadline notice with the renewal amount and cancellation channels, or the renewal provision is unenforceable.
laws.scope: Consumer "service contracts" (written contracts for the performance of services over a fixed period or specified duration for personal, family or household purposes) whose automatic renewal provision renews for more than one month and keeps the contract in effect more than six months after it began (§ 37-1-301(31)-(32)). Telecommunications and broadband renewals are excluded. Sanction: the automatic renewal provision is unenforceable.

Violations are TCPA violations.
laws.scope: Consumers (personal, family or household purposes). Exempt: FDIC-insured banks and trust companies, NCUA-insured credit unions, Department of Financial Institutions licensees, franchised or TPUC/FCC/FERC-regulated services, and title 56 insurance licensees.

amendments.summary: Affirmative-consent definition; sixty-day charge-date notice; seven-day refund-on-request remedy.

laws.statute: Utah Automatic Renewal Contracts Act
laws.summary: Notice duties only: 30-60 days before renewals into a paid term longer than 45 days (renewal date, total cost, cancellation options) and at least 3 days before any free trial expires. Non-compliant renewal provisions are void.
laws.scope: Exempt: insurance-regulated persons, service contracts, GLBA-regulated financial institutions, public utilities, FCC/FERC-regulated services, rental agreements and property management agreements.

amendments.summary: Cross-reference and enforcement updates to §§ 13-70-101 and -301 (no change to notice duties).

enforcement.remedies: Non-compliant renewal provisions are void; Division of Consumer Protection administrative fines and civil penalties up to $2,500 per violation.

laws.statute: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
laws.summary: Contracts of one year or longer renewing for more than a month: bold-face plain-language renewal terms; separate opt-in; 30-60 day notice; cancellation mechanism; online termination for online contracts. Violations are unfair and deceptive acts (§ 2453).
laws.scope: Applies only to consumer contracts with an initial term of one year or longer that renew for a subsequent term longer than one month. Without compliance the contract does not renew automatically. Exempt: financial institutions, credit unions and insurance contracts.

amendments.summary: Cancellation mechanism and online termination; revised notice contents.

enforcement.remedies: Vermont Consumer Protection Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

laws.statute: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
laws.summary: Offer terms next to consent (strict clear-and-conspicuous standard online); affirmative consent; acknowledgment; cancellation at least as easy as sign-up through every sign-up channel with no required agent; material-change notice; free-trial notice within the last 30 days of trials over 30 days; 30-60 day notice for renewals extending more than 12 months. Violations are VCPA prohibited practices.
laws.scope: "Consumer" includes small businesses (independently owned, 250 or fewer employees or $10 million or less in receipts). Exempt (§ 59.1-207.48): franchised/SCC-, FCC- or FERC-regulated services, banks and other licensed financial institutions, insurers.

amendments.summary: Conspicuous online cancellation option for online sellers; trial acknowledgment wording.
"Automatic renewal" limited to renewal terms of more than one month.
Free-trial notice for trials over 30 days.
30-60 day renewal notice; timing of disclosures and material-change notice.
Cancellation-mechanism rewrite (as easy as sign-up, every channel, no required agent, phone rules); "seller"; clear-and-conspicuous standard.

enforcement.remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

laws.statute: New York City "Click to Cancel" Rule (DCWP)
laws.summary: City rule mirroring GBL § 527-a: material terms (including the deadline to act) before consent or billing information; cancellation as easy as consent, in the same medium and every consent medium, with an online option (website or email) for in-person sign-ups; no obstruction or unreasonable save offers; 15-45 day renewal notice (initial term of one year or more renewing for six months or more) and 3-21 day trial notice (trials over a month) in the consumer-selected channel; 5 business day-30 day material-change notice. Violators refund every amount charged after the first cancellation attempt (§ 5-110.2); DCWP penalties $525 / $1,050 / $3,500. Evaluated under US-NY (the jurisdiction model has no city level).
laws.scope: New York City consumers. Exempt (§ 5-110.3): municipal franchise holders (e.g. cable), DFS-regulated entities, licensed alarm operators, banks and licensed financial institutions, and service-contract sellers. Territorial reach and interaction with state AG enforcement are open question 9 (hence medium confidence).

enforcement.remedies: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection: penalties of $525 (first), $1,050 (second) and $3,500 (third and later) per violation, and restitution of every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel (6 RCNY § 5-110.2).

requirements.law: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act (ROSCA)
requirements.title: Clearly and conspicuously disclose all material terms before obtaining billing information
requirements.summary: Before collecting the consumer's billing information, the seller must provide text that clearly and conspicuously discloses all material terms of the transaction: that the consumer will be charged on a recurring basis until they cancel, the amount and frequency of the charges, any free-trial length and the charge after it, and how to cancel.

exposure.remedies: ROSCA: FTC and state attorneys general only. Violations are treated as FTC rule violations: civil penalties up to $53,088 per violation (counted per consumer) and consumer redress (e.g. Amazon $2.5B, Adobe $150M).

exposure.remedies: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection: penalties of $525 (first), $1,050 (second) and $3,500 (third and later) per violation, and restitution of every amount charged after the consumer's first attempt to cancel (6 RCNY § 5-110.2).

requirements.law: Alaska free trial period law

requirements.summary: When offering, promoting or advertising goods or services for a free trial period, clearly and conspicuously disclose all material terms: restrictions, limitations and conditions (including any minimum purchase obligation after the trial), a description of all charges imposed after the trial (including shipping and handling), the consumer's right to cancel, and any other obligations assumed by accepting the trial.

exposure.remedies: Unfair trade practice under AS 45.50.471(b)(47); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Alaska free trial period law
requirements.title: Allow cancellation during the trial and a refund within 30 days after it ends

exposure.remedies: Unfair trade practice under AS 45.50.471(b)(47); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

exposure.remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.summary: Maintain verification of the consumer's consent for at least three years, or one year after the contract is terminated, whichever is longer.

exposure.remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)

exposure.remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
requirements.title: Notice before a free trial or promotional price longer than 31 days ends
requirements.summary: If the consumer accepted a free gift or trial (or promotional price) lasting more than 31 days, send the § 4-86-112(b)(8) notice — renewal statement, renewal length and terms, amount/range and frequency of charges, cancellation methods, a cancellation link if sent electronically, contact information — 3 to 21 days before the period expires.

exposure.remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
requirements.title: Renewal notice for initial terms of one year or longer
requirements.summary: For an initial term of one year or longer, send the § 4-86-112(b)(8) notice 15 to 45 days before the subscription renews.

exposure.remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
requirements.title: Cancellation mechanism; phone lines answered promptly; voicemail handled within one business day
requirements.summary: Provide a toll-free number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism, described in the acknowledgment. exposure.remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
requirements.title: Online sign-ups must be able to cancel online, at will, immediately

exposure.remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.title: Save offers only with a continuously displayed "click to cancel" option

exposure.remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Arkansas automatic renewal and continuous service offers law (Act 652 of 2025)
requirements.title: Cancellation in the same medium used to sign up

exposure.remedies: Enforced under the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
requirements.title: Present the automatic renewal offer terms clearly and conspicuously before the contract is executed
requirements.summary: Before the contract is executed, clearly and conspicuously present the automatic renewal offer terms: that the contract will renew or extend after the initial period for a set term not exceeding one year (unless the consumer gives express written consent to a longer term); the cancellation policy; any recurring charges; the length of the renewal term; and any minimum purchase obligation. Voice offers: in temporal proximity to the consent request. Trial offers must also clearly and conspicuously explain the price and any further purchase obligations after the trial.

exposure.remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

requirements.law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
requirements.title: Links to renewal details must be adjacent to the purchase link and labelled as an auto-renewal enrollment
requirements.summary: An online link to detailed automatic-renewal information may be used only if it is available before the consumer elects to purchase, appears directly adjacent to the link used to purchase, and is labelled with (or directly adjacent to) a clear and conspicuous statement that by purchasing the consumer agrees to enroll in an automatic renewal contract.

exposure.remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

requirements.law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
requirements.title: Send a retainable written acknowledgment; for trials explain how to cancel before paying
requirements.summary: Provide a written acknowledgment, retainable by the consumer, with the automatic renewal offer terms, the cancellation policy and how to cancel. For trial offers, explain how to cancel and allow cancellation before the consumer must pay.

exposure.remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

requirements.law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
requirements.title: One-step online cancellation link
requirements.summary: Provide a simple, cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use and readily accessible cancellation mechanism. Safe harbor: for consumers who consented online or through an electronic communication, a one-step online cancellation link — on the website, in the device or service, or in an electronic communication — available immediately after a reasonable authentication used solely to confirm authority over the account; for other consents, a one-step online link or a qualifying in-person mechanism where the consumer regularly uses the goods or services. "One-step online cancellation" means no additional action that obstructs or delays immediate termination.

exposure.remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

requirements.law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
requirements.title: Online save offers only with a continuously displayed direct cancel link
requirements.summary: When a consumer cancels online, a discounted offer, retention benefit or information about the effects of cancelling may be shown only if a prominently located, continuously proximate direct link to cancel is displayed alongside it; if the consumer uses that link the cancellation must be processed promptly without further obstruction or delay.

exposure.remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

requirements.law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law
requirements.title: Notice of material changes with cancellation information

notice_window.description: any time before the price change

exposure.remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

requirements.law: Colorado automatic renewal contracts law

exposure.remedies: Enforced exclusively by the Attorney General and district attorneys.

requirements.law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law

Continuous-service terms must be disclosed before the consumer enters the agreement; automatic-renewal terms "before such automatic renewal".

exposure.remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

requirements.law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
requirements.title: Disclose the post-trial price before the consumer enters the agreement

exposure.remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

exposure.remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

requirements.title: Notice during free trials or promotional periods of 32 days or more

Timing: for periods of at least 32 days, at least 21 days after the period starts and "not earlier than three days before" it expires; for periods of at least one year, 15 to 45 days before it expires.

exposure.remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

exposure.remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

requirements.law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
requirements.title: Online agreements must be cancellable online without any offline step or obstruction
requirements.summary: A business that enters into an agreement online must let the consumer take every action needed to stop renewal or terminate the service online, without requiring offline action, and may not obstruct or delay those efforts. requirements.title: Cancel by prominent link/button, reply email, or a retainable phone number shown on the website
requirements.summary: Every business with an automatic renewal or continuous services agreement must let consumers cancel by a prominently displayed direct link or button (in the account/profile or device/user settings), an immediately accessible email the consumer can reply to without more information, or a retainable telephone number clearly and conspicuously displayed on the business's website.

exposure.remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

requirements.law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
requirements.title: No obstruction; phone line and voicemail rules; phone save offers only after the "say cancel" disclosure
requirements.summary: Do not obstruct or delay cancellation. A cancellation phone line must be answered promptly during normal business hours; a cancellation voicemail must be processed (or the call returned) within one business day, and processed within one business day if the consumer cannot be reached and the voicemail has enough information. On calls, retention offers may be made only after clearly telling the consumer they can cancel at any time by saying "cancel".

exposure.remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

requirements.law: Connecticut automatic renewal and continuous services law
requirements.title: Annual reminder for every automatic renewal or continuous services agreement
requirements.summary: From July 1, 2026, send each consumer an annual reminder identifying the goods or services, how to stop renewal or terminate, and the frequency and amount of the charges — in the manner the subscription was activated (if not in person) or the consumer's usual channel, otherwise by email, mail or phone.

exposure.remedies: A violation is a CUTPA unfair trade practice (the former "no private right of action" clause was deleted); private CUTPA suits are likely; a vendor claim of a new express private right is unverified.

requirements.law: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
requirements.title: Disclose the automatic renewal provision and cancellation procedure clearly and conspicuously
requirements.summary: A contract that automatically renews at the end of a definite term must disclose the automatic renewal provision and the cancellation procedure clearly and conspicuously in the contract, visually proximate to any request for consent.

exposure.remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

requirements.law: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
requirements.title: Explain the post-trial price
requirements.summary: If the offer includes a free gift or trial, clearly and conspicuously explain the price charged after the trial ends or how the subscription price will change when it ends.

exposure.remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

requirements.law: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
requirements.title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline (12-month+ initial terms), every year
requirements.summary: For an initial term of 12 months or more that renews for one month or more, notify the consumer of the first renewal and annually thereafter, 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, by first-class mail, email, or another accessible form the consumer authorized, disclosing clearly and conspicuously: that it will renew unless cancelled; the cost for the renewal term; the cancellation deadline; and how to get details of the renewal and cancellation procedures. Email notices must include active links to cancel.

exposure.remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

requirements.law: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
requirements.title: Trial notice 15-30 days before a free trial of one month or more ends
requirements.summary: For a free trial with a term of one month or more that automatically renews when the trial ends, notify the consumer of the automatic renewal 15 to 30 days before the trial expires.

exposure.remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

requirements.law: Automatic Renewal Protections Act of 2018
requirements.title: Separate affirmative consent to the automatic renewal after a free trial
requirements.summary: Notwithstanding the consumer's consent to the free trial, obtain the consumer's affirmative consent to the automatic renewal before charging for it.

exposure.remedies: Violations void the renewal provision and violate the Consumer Protection Procedures Act (CPPA; good-faith-error defense); private CPPA suits are likely.

requirements.law: Delaware consumer contracts — automatic renewal provisions
requirements.title: Disclose the automatic renewal terms clearly and conspicuously when the contract is made
requirements.summary: A seller whose consumer contract contains an automatic renewal provision must disclose the terms of that provision clearly and conspicuously at the time the contract is entered into.

exposure.remedies: Private suit with treble damages; renewals in violation are voidable; 30-day notice-and-cure before consumer suits.

requirements.law: Delaware consumer contracts — automatic renewal provisions
requirements.title: Notice of each extension 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline
requirements.summary: For a contract renewed for more than one month at a time where the renewal keeps it in effect more than 12 months after it began, notify the consumer of each upcoming extension 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, disclosing clearly and conspicuously: that it will renew unless cancelled; the date by which to cancel; the procedure to cancel (an online procedure if the consumer contracted online); and how to obtain the renewal provision details.

exposure.remedies: Private suit with treble damages; renewals in violation are voidable; 30-day notice-and-cure before consumer suits.

requirements.law: Delaware consumer contracts — automatic renewal provisions
requirements.title: Easy cancellation for any auto-renewing contract; online sign-ups cancel online
requirements.summary: For any contract that automatically renews — regardless of the renewal period — failing to provide a cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism is a deceptive practice; a consumer who contracted online must be allowed to cancel online.

exposure.remedies: Private suit with treble damages; renewals in violation are voidable; 30-day notice-and-cure before consumer suits.

requirements.law: Florida automatic renewal of service contracts
requirements.title: Disclose the automatic renewal provision clearly and conspicuously in the contract or offer
requirements.summary: A seller of a service contract with an automatic renewal provision must disclose the provision clearly and conspicuously in the contract or contract offer.

exposure.remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Florida automatic renewal of service contracts
requirements.title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline for 12-month+ service contracts
requirements.summary: For a service contract with a term of 12 months or more that renews for more than one month, give written or electronic notice of the automatic renewal provision 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, disclosing clearly and conspicuously that the contract will renew unless cancelled and how to obtain details of the renewal provision and the cancellation procedure.

exposure.remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Florida automatic renewal of service contracts
requirements.title: Allow cancellation in the same manner and by the same means as acceptance
requirements.summary: A seller that enters into or renews a service contract with an automatic renewal provision must allow the consumer to cancel in the same manner, and by the same means, as the consumer accepted the contract.

exposure.remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
requirements.title: Present the offer terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request
requirements.summary: Before the subscription is fulfilled, present the offer terms — the cancellation policy, the recurring charges (and any known change in amount), the length of the renewal term or that the service is continuous, and any minimum purchase obligation — clearly and conspicuously and in visual proximity to the request for consent.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

requirements.law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
requirements.title: Obtain consent before charging
requirements.summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or third-party payment account without first obtaining the consumer's consent to the agreement containing the offer terms.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

requirements.law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
requirements.title: Send an easily retained acknowledgment with the offer terms, cancellation policy and how to cancel
requirements.summary: Provide an acknowledgment of the offer terms (on the business's website, via a link to platform-specific instructions, or otherwise in a manner easily retained), including the cancellation policy and how to cancel and a description of the cancellation mechanism (toll-free number, email, postal address if billing directly, or another cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use mechanism). It may follow the initial order.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

requirements.law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
requirements.title: Charge notice before or within three days after charging
requirements.summary: Unless the consumer opted out, send a notice before charging the consumer or within three days after the charge, stating clearly and conspicuously: that the subscription will automatically renew unless cancelled; the length and other terms of the renewal period; a link or other electronic way to reach the cancellation process (if sent electronically); and the business's contact information.

notice_window.description: before the charge or up to 3 days after it

exposure.remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

requirements.law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
requirements.title: Online sign-ups must be able to cancel online; describe the cancellation mechanism
requirements.summary: A business that lets consumers accept online must let them cancel online, e.g. via a clear and conspicuous link to a website or online cancellation service or a pre-formatted cancellation email; it may require account authentication, with an offline alternative for consumers who cannot authenticate online. It must also provide a toll-free number, email, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use mechanism.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

requirements.law: Georgia Online Automatic Renewal Transparency Act
requirements.title: Notice of material changes with cancellation information
requirements.summary: For a material change in an accepted online offer, provide a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and easily retained information on how to cancel.

notice_window.description: any time before the price change

exposure.remedies: Attorney General only (injunction, restitution); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties; no private right of action.

requirements.law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
requirements.title: Disclose the automatic renewal clause and cancellation procedure clearly and conspicuously
requirements.summary: For a consumer contract with a term of more than one month that automatically renews for more than one month, disclose the automatic renewal clause and the cancellation procedure clearly and conspicuously in the contract.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
requirements.title: Disclose the continuous service clause and cancellation procedure clearly and conspicuously
requirements.summary: For a consumer contract with a continuous service clause (continues until cancelled), clearly and conspicuously disclose the clause and the cancellation procedure.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
requirements.title: Obtain affirmative consent before charging
requirements.summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or third-party account for an automatic renewal or continuous service without first obtaining affirmative consent to the agreement containing the offer terms.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
requirements.title: Send a retainable acknowledgment; for trials state the right to cancel before paying
requirements.summary: Provide an acknowledgment the consumer may retain with the offer terms, cancellation policy and cancellation procedure. For free trials it must also clearly and conspicuously state the right to cancel before payment and how.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
requirements.title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline (12-month+ contracts)
requirements.summary: For a contract term of 12 months or more that renews for more than one month, notify the consumer clearly and conspicuously that it will renew unless cancelled, how to cancel, and the deadline to respond, 30 to 60 days before that deadline. Electronic notice is allowed if the sale was electronic (UETA) or the consumer elected email notices.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
requirements.title: Provide a cancellation channel and honor cancellation requests
requirements.summary: Include a toll-free number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or a clearly and conspicuously described cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use alternative to communicate cancellation; knowingly failing to cancel upon the consumer's request is an unfair or deceptive practice.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Hawaii automatic renewal and continuous service clauses law
requirements.title: Notice of material changes before implementation
requirements.summary: Before implementing a material change, clearly and conspicuously notify Hawaii consumers of the change with retainable information on how to cancel.

notice_window.description: any time before the price change

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Idaho cancellation of subscriptions law
requirements.title: Clearly and conspicuously disclose the renewal terms and the ways to cancel
requirements.summary: An online automatic subscription renewal offer must clearly and conspicuously disclose the automatic renewal terms and the methods the consumer may use to cancel.

exposure.remedies: Idaho Consumer Protection Act violation: Attorney General enforcement, no private right of action; good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Idaho cancellation of subscriptions law
requirements.title: Offer a free, easy online cancellation mechanism; phone numbers must be toll-free and prominent
requirements.summary: Provide cancellation methods that include a cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use online mechanism (which may be a pre-formatted termination email), without an additional cancellation fee; any cancellation phone number must be toll-free and prominently displayed in the disclosure.

exposure.remedies: Idaho Consumer Protection Act violation: Attorney General enforcement, no private right of action; good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Idaho cancellation of subscriptions law
requirements.title: Renewal notice 30-60 days ahead for subscriptions renewing for 12 months or more
requirements.summary: For an extended automatic subscription renewal (renewing for a term of 12 months or more), notify the consumer 30 to 60 days before the goods or services are delivered or provided, clearly and conspicuously describing them, stating the price, saying they will be provided unless the consumer declines, and giving one or more cancellation methods (including at least one at no cost), with the same online cancellation methods as § 48-603G(3).

exposure.remedies: Idaho Consumer Protection Act violation: Attorney General enforcement, no private right of action; good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act

requirements.title: Obtain consent before charging

exposure.remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

requirements.law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act

exposure.remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

requirements.law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
requirements.title: Notice during a free trial or promotional period of 15 days or more

exposure.remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

requirements.law: Illinois Automatic Contract Renewal Act
requirements.title: Written renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline (12-month+ contracts)

exposure.remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

requirements.title: Online offers: cancellation mechanism, and online sign-ups can cancel exclusively online

exposure.remedies: Violations are Consumer Fraud Act (ICFA) violations: private suits with attorney's-fee shifting (FloSports $1.55M); forecast to lead the 2026-27 multistate wave.

requirements.title: Send a retainable acknowledgment describing how to cancel; trials cancellable before payment

requirements.law: Kentucky automatic renewal and continuous service offers law

requirements.title: Disclose clearly and conspicuously how to cancel

requirements.law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act

requirements.law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act

requirements.law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act

exposure.remedies: Attorney General only: civil penalty up to $500 per violation after a 30-day cure period.

requirements.law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
requirements.title: Send a retainable acknowledgment; for trials or discounts explain how to cancel before being charged

requirements.law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act

requirements.law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act
requirements.title: Notice of material changes, including price increases, before the renewal at which they apply

requirements.law: Louisiana Click-to-Cancel Act

exposure.remedies: Unfair and deceptive practice under M.G.L. c. 93A: private actions for double or treble damages and attorney's fees (after a 30-day demand letter); AG enforcement.

requirements.law: Massachusetts Attorney General regulation — Unfair and Deceptive Fees (recurring fees and trial offers)

exposure.remedies: Unfair and deceptive practice under M.G.L. c. 93A: private actions for double or treble damages and attorney's fees (after a 30-day demand letter); AG enforcement.
