requirements.law: Massachusetts Attorney General regulation — Unfair and Deceptive Fees (recurring fees and trial offers)
requirements.title: Plans of 31 days or less: pre-deadline notice or a per-charge notice with cancel instructions
requirements.summary: For negative option contracts of 31 days or less (e.g. monthly plans), either send the 940 CMR 38.05(4) notice, or, at least as often as the consumer is charged, a written notice disclosing clearly and conspicuously the amount charged at renewal and how to cancel to avoid further charges, through a similar or commonly used medium.

notice_window.description: up to 30 days before the charge or up to 3 days after it

exposure.remedies: Unfair and deceptive practice under M.G.L. c. 93A: private actions for double or treble damages and attorney's fees (after a 30-day demand letter); AG enforcement.

requirements.law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
requirements.title: Present the renewal terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request
requirements.summary: Before the subscription is fulfilled, present the automatic renewal offer terms — including the price charged after the initial term ends or how the agreement will change at the end of it — clearly and conspicuously and in visual proximity to the request for consent (for oral offers, at the same time as the request).

exposure.remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

requirements.law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
requirements.title: Disclose the cancellation methods in an easily accessible way
requirements.summary: Present the consumer with an easily accessible disclosure of the methods the consumer may use to cancel the automatic renewal.

exposure.remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

requirements.law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
requirements.title: Explain the post-trial price
requirements.summary: If the offer includes a free gift or trial, clearly and conspicuously explain the price charged after the trial and how pricing will change at its end.

exposure.remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

requirements.law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
requirements.title: Notice and consent before automatically charging a credit card (initial terms over one month)
requirements.summary: For an automatic renewal offer with an initial definite term of more than one month, do not automatically charge the consumer's credit card unless clear and conspicuous notice is given and the consumer consents to the automatic charge.

exposure.remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

requirements.law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
requirements.title: Cancellation as easy as sign-up, same medium, prominent link/button or email, no required live agent
requirements.summary: Provide a cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use mechanism to cancel, avoid (increased) charges and immediately stop recurring charges, without unreasonable delay, hindrance or obstruction. It must be at least as easy as the consent mechanism and available in the same medium. Online cancellation must be easy to find, must not require talking to a live or virtual representative (unless sign-up did), and must include a prominently placed direct link or button (in the account/profile or device/user settings) or an immediately accessible pre-formatted termination email. Phone cancellation must be performed promptly on a number that is answered or records messages during business hours; in-person cancellation must resemble the in-person sign-up and also offer the online and phone options.

exposure.remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

requirements.law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
requirements.title: Notice 3-21 days before a free gift or trial longer than 14 days converts
requirements.summary: If the offer includes a free gift or trial lasting more than 14 days, give a clear and conspicuous notice 3 to 21 days before the automatic renewal takes effect, stating: that it will renew unless cancelled; the duration and terms of the renewal (including the post-trial price); the ways to cancel; a cancellation link if sent electronically; and contact information.

exposure.remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

requirements.law: Maryland Consumer Protection — Automatic Renewals (2025 chs. 204, 205)
requirements.title: Renewal notice 15-45 days ahead for initial terms of at least one year
requirements.summary: If the consumer accepted an initial term of at least one year, give the § 14-1329(c)(1) notice 15 to 45 days before the automatic renewal takes effect.

exposure.remedies: Unfair, abusive or deceptive trade practice (Consumer Protection Act Title 13); the statute says there is no private right of action under this section.

requirements.law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
requirements.title: Clear, conspicuous and easily accessible disclosure of all material terms and the ways to cancel
requirements.summary: Present a clear, conspicuous and easily accessible disclosure of all material terms of the renewal offer — including the amount and frequency of charges and the refund policy on cancellation — and of the methods the consumer may use to cancel; any cancellation phone number must be toll-free and prominently displayed in the disclosure. No misrepresentation of material facts about the renewal offer.

exposure.remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
requirements.title: Express consent to the renewal by check box, e-signature or other affirmative action
requirements.summary: Before enrollment, obtain the consumer's express consent to the automatic renewal through a check box, electronic signature or other affirmative action agreeing to the renewal offer.

exposure.remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
requirements.title: Cancellation by the same method and in the same manner as sign-up
requirements.summary: Provide for cancellation of the subscription or membership using the same method, and in the same manner, by which the consumer initially agreed to it (an online sign-up must be cancellable online).

exposure.remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
requirements.title: Renewal notice no more than 30 days before renewal for 12-month+ subscriptions
requirements.summary: For an extended renewal (subscription term of 12 months or more renewing for more than one month), notify the consumer no more than 30 days before the renewal date, disclosing clearly and conspicuously that it will renew unless cancelled and where to obtain details of the renewal and cancellation procedure.

exposure.remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
requirements.title: Disclose the ways to cancel and provide online cancellation (2020-2025 text)
requirements.summary: A seller may not make an automatic subscription renewal offer without an easily accessible disclosure of the methods the consumer may use to cancel; the seller must provide for online cancellation; any cancellation phone number must be toll-free and prominently displayed in the disclosure.

exposure.remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Maine automatic subscription or health club membership renewal law
requirements.title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline for 12-month+ subscriptions (2020-2025 text)
requirements.summary: For an extended automatic subscription renewal (term of 12 months or more renewing for more than one month), notify the consumer 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, disclosing clearly and conspicuously that it will renew unless cancelled and where to obtain details of the renewal and cancellation procedure; online cancellation required.

exposure.remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Maine charges after free trial period
requirements.title: Free offers: get billing information directly from the consumer and disclose the free-offer terms
requirements.summary: A seller may not make a free offer (one that obligates the consumer to pay unless they contact the seller) unless, when the consumer agrees, the seller obtains the billing information directly from the consumer and clearly and conspicuously discloses the terms of the free offer, including any additional financial obligations.

exposure.remedies: Treble refund of amounts charged in violation (§ 1210-D); Attorney General enforcement; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
requirements.title: Present the offer terms clearly and conspicuously before acceptance, next to the offer
requirements.summary: Before the consumer accepts, present the offer terms (§ 325G.56, subd. 7): that the agreement continues until the consumer terminates it; the cancellation policy; the recurring charges (and any change); the renewal term or that service is continuous (unless chosen by the consumer); and any minimum purchase obligation, clearly and conspicuously and in visual (or, for voice offers, temporal) proximity to the offer.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
requirements.title: No charges before the agreement is authorized; consent required
requirements.summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or third-party account before the agreement has been duly authorized by the seller and consumer and made effective; goods sent without the consumer's affirmative consent are an unconditional gift.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
requirements.title: Timely retainable confirmation with the terms, trial cancellation and termination options
requirements.summary: In a timely manner after acceptance, send a retainable confirmation (email suffices) with the offer terms; for free trials, how to cancel before paying; and easy, cost-effective, timely termination options, including the website termination election for online sellers and, for sign-ups by other means, an option as easy and accessible as the original means of acceptance.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
requirements.title: Notice of material changes before implementation (otherwise the change is void)
requirements.summary: Before implementing a material change, give a timely, clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to terminate; a material change made without it is void and unenforceable.

notice_window.description: any time before the price change

exposure.remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
requirements.title: Notice 5-30 days before a free trial longer than 30 days ends
requirements.summary: If the offer includes a free trial lasting more than 30 days, notify the consumer 5 to 30 days before the trial ends of the option to cancel before the trial ends to avoid paying.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
requirements.title: Yearly written notice for continuous-service subscriptions
requirements.summary: For a continuous-service agreement, give the consumer written notice of the continuous service by mail or email at least once per calendar year, including the terms of the service and how to terminate or manage it.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
requirements.title: No retention offers after a cancellation request unless the consumer opts in; no abusive tactics
requirements.summary: After receiving a cancellation or termination notice, the seller may not misrepresent or use unfair or abusive tactics to delay or avoid cancellation, and may not make retention offers, benefits, modifications or gifts unless the consumer grants permission after giving notice (asked only once per attempt). The seller may ask (without requiring an answer) why the consumer is cancelling, explain consequences, verify identity, and describe downgrade, pause or suspension options.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
requirements.title: Website "termination election" for sellers with account or subscription management
requirements.summary: A seller whose website has profile or subscription-management capabilities must include a clear and conspicuous termination election that tells consumers in plain language they can terminate at any time, asks only for information needed to process the termination, and uses a checkbox, submit button or similarly simple mechanism — regardless of how the consumer signed up.

exposure.remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: Minnesota automatic renewal and continuous service law
requirements.title: Honor terminations: end of term for renewals; within 31 days for continuous service
requirements.summary: A consumer may terminate at any time using the procedure in the confirmation. Automatic-renewal terminations take effect at the end of the current term (or a later term the consumer picks); continuous-service terminations must take effect no later than 31 days after a verified notice (unless the consumer chooses a later date).

exposure.remedies: Attorney General enforcement; a private action is likely available through Minnesota's private attorney general statute (unverified); good-faith compliance bars civil penalties.

requirements.law: North Carolina contracts with automatic renewal clauses
requirements.title: Disclose the automatic renewal clause clearly and conspicuously
requirements.summary: Disclose the automatic renewal clause clearly and conspicuously in the contract or contract offer.

exposure.remedies: The automatic renewal clause is void and unenforceable (§ 75-41(e)); good-faith-error defense with full refund; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: North Carolina contracts with automatic renewal clauses
requirements.title: Disclose clearly and conspicuously how to cancel
requirements.summary: Disclose clearly and conspicuously how to cancel the contract in the initial contract, the contract offer, or with delivery of the products or services.

exposure.remedies: The automatic renewal clause is void and unenforceable (§ 75-41(e)); good-faith-error defense with full refund; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: North Carolina contracts with automatic renewal clauses
requirements.title: Written renewal notice 15-45 days before renewals longer than 60 days
requirements.summary: For any automatic renewal exceeding 60 days, give written notice by personal delivery, email or first-class mail 15 to 45 days before the renewal date, stating the date the contract will renew and that it will renew unless cancelled before then.

exposure.remedies: The automatic renewal clause is void and unenforceable (§ 75-41(e)); good-faith-error defense with full refund; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: North Carolina contracts with automatic renewal clauses
requirements.title: Changed terms at renewal must be disclosed in the renewal notice in 12-point bold type
requirements.summary: If the contract terms will change upon automatic renewal, disclose the changing terms clearly and conspicuously in the renewal notification, in at least 12-point type and in bold print.

exposure.remedies: The automatic renewal clause is void and unenforceable (§ 75-41(e)); good-faith-error defense with full refund; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
requirements.title: Present the automatic renewal terms clearly and conspicuously, near the offer
requirements.summary: Present the terms of the automatic renewal offer clearly and conspicuously before the subscription or purchase agreement is fulfilled and in proximity to the offer.

exposure.remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

requirements.law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
requirements.title: No charge without compliant disclosures and affirmative consent
requirements.summary: Do not charge the buyer's card, bank account or other financial account unless the § 51-37-02(1) requirements are met and the buyer gave affirmative consent to the agreement containing the automatic renewal terms.

exposure.remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

requirements.law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
requirements.title: Renewal periods may not exceed twelve months
requirements.summary: The renewal period in an automatic renewal provision may not exceed twelve months.

exposure.remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

requirements.law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
requirements.title: Retainable acknowledgment with the terms and a simple cancellation procedure
requirements.summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the automatic renewal terms and how to cancel, describing a cost-effective, timely and simple cancellation procedure.

exposure.remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

requirements.law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
requirements.title: Provide a cost-effective, timely and simple cancellation procedure
requirements.summary: Provide a cost-effective, timely and simple procedure for cancellation, described in the acknowledgment.

exposure.remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

requirements.law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
requirements.title: Written renewal notice 30-60 days ahead for renewal periods over six months
requirements.summary: If the agreement renews for a period of more than six months, give clear and conspicuous written notice (first-class mail, email, or text/app if the consumer authorized it) that the buyer may cancel and avoid renewal, with the cancellation procedure, 30 to 60 days before the renewal date or the end of the cancellation period.

exposure.remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

requirements.law: North Dakota customer contract clauses and automatic renewals
requirements.title: Notice of material changes with cancellation information
requirements.summary: If the terms materially change, give clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to cancel.

notice_window.description: any time before the price change

exposure.remedies: A non-compliant automatic renewal provision is void, and goods or services provided under it (or after an attempted cancellation) are unconditional gifts (§ 51-37-04); Attorney General and private enforcement.

requirements.law: New Mexico rule — Automatic Renewal of Service Contracts
requirements.title: Set out the automatic renewal provision clearly and conspicuously in at least 10-point type
requirements.summary: A consumer service contract may contain an automatic renewal provision only if it is set forth clearly and conspicuously in at least 10-point type and states the notice requirements, the specific procedure to cancel at the end of the initial term, and the renewal terms that apply if no cancellation notice is given.

exposure.remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: New Mexico rule — Automatic Renewal of Service Contracts
requirements.title: Written renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline, by certified mail or on a monthly statement
requirements.summary: Before the end of the initial term and of each renewal term, serve written notice specifying the cancellation procedure, clearly and conspicuously in at least 10-point type, by certified mail or on the first page of a monthly statement, 30 to 60 days before the last day on which the consumer may give notice of termination.

exposure.remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: New Mexico rule — Automatic Renewal of Service Contracts
requirements.title: Honor timely cancellation notices sent by any reliable means; no termination cost
requirements.summary: Allow at least 30 calendar days after the consumer receives the renewal notice to give notice of termination; honor cancellation notices sent by fax, mail, email or other reliable means (including timely-sent notices received late); and allow termination at the end of the initial or any renewal term without additional cost or penalty.

exposure.remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
requirements.title: Present the offer terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request
requirements.summary: Before the subscription is fulfilled, present the offer terms (ORS 646A.293(5)): that the subscription continues until the consumer cancels; the cancellation policy; the recurring charges (and the new amount if it will change, if known); the renewal term length or that service is continuous; and any minimum purchase obligation, clearly and conspicuously and in visual (or, for voice offers, temporal) proximity to the request for consent.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
requirements.title: Obtain affirmative consent before charging
requirements.summary: Do not charge the consumer's card or third-party payment account without first obtaining affirmative consent to the agreement containing the offer terms; goods sent without it are an unconditional gift.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
requirements.title: Send a retainable acknowledgment; free trials cancellable before payment
requirements.summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the offer terms and how to cancel (it may follow the initial order). For free trials, the acknowledgment must explain how to cancel, and the consumer must be allowed to cancel before paying.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
requirements.title: Provide a cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism
requirements.summary: Provide a toll-free number, email address, post-office address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism, described in the acknowledgment.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Oregon automatic renewal and continuous service offers law
requirements.title: Notice of material changes before implementation
requirements.summary: Before implementing a material change, give a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to cancel.

notice_window.description: any time before the price change

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Oregon free offer law
requirements.title: Free offers: clear and conspicuous terms in close proximity to the consent request
requirements.summary: Before the consumer accepts a free offer that leads to a financial obligation, provide clear and conspicuous information, in close proximity to the consent request: all goods, services or enrollments the consumer will be obligated for; the cost; any need to take affirmative action to reject and how; that the consumer will be obligated unless they cancel; the right to cancel by toll-free call or in a manner substantially similar to acceptance; the time by which to cancel; and any return-credit rights.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Oregon free offer law
requirements.title: Free offers: billing information directly from the consumer and affirmative consent
requirements.summary: Obtain billing information directly from the consumer (or with affirmative consent to its transfer) and obtain the consumer's affirmative consent to the free-offer terms before imposing any financial obligation.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Oregon free offer law
requirements.title: Free offers: honor cancellation via the disclosed toll-free or same-manner procedure
requirements.summary: Do not fail or refuse to cancel a free offer when the consumer uses (or reasonably tries to use) the cancellation procedure — a toll-free number or a method substantially similar to how the consumer accepted.

exposure.remedies: California-style law; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: South Carolina automatic renewal provisions in service contracts
requirements.title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the cancellation deadline, with the renewal amount and how to cancel
requirements.summary: An automatic renewal provision in a service contract is unenforceable unless the consumer received written or electronic notice 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline, conspicuously disclosing: that the contract will renew unless cancelled; the amount charged on renewal; and how to get details of the renewal and cancellation procedure, including a toll-free number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism.

exposure.remedies: Remedy: the automatic-renewal provision is void / unenforceable; whether this "service contract" law reaches digital subscriptions at all is unsettled (open question 16); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
requirements.title: Present the renewal terms clearly and conspicuously next to the consent request; explain post-trial pricing
requirements.summary: Before the agreement is fulfilled, present the automatic renewal or continuous service offer terms (continues until cancelled; cancellation policy; recurring charges and any change; term length or continuous; minimum purchase obligation) clearly and conspicuously and in visual (or temporal) proximity to the consent request; for free gifts or trials, clearly and conspicuously explain the post-trial price.

exposure.remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
requirements.title: Obtain affirmative consent (a clear, specific, informed, unambiguous act) before charging
requirements.summary: Before charging the consumer's card or third-party account, obtain affirmative consent to the agreement containing the offer terms (including promotional-price terms) — "a clear, affirmative act signifying a consumer's freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous agreement", such as a written (including electronic) statement or an unambiguous affirmative action. A charge made without it must be refunded if the consumer asks within seven days of the charge.

exposure.remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
requirements.title: Charge-date notice when a trial ends more than 60 days after sign-up
requirements.summary: If the automatic renewal will occur more than 60 days after affirmative consent (e.g. a long free trial), the entity billing the consumer must give a clear and conspicuous notice of when the consumer will be charged.

notice_window.description: any time before the trial ends

exposure.remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
requirements.title: Charge-date notice when the first renewal is more than 60 days after sign-up
requirements.summary: If the first automatic renewal will occur more than 60 days after affirmative consent (terms of about two months or longer), the entity billing the consumer must give a clear and conspicuous notice of when the consumer will be charged for the renewal.

exposure.remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
requirements.title: Send a retainable acknowledgment describing how to cancel; trials cancellable before payment
requirements.summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the offer terms, cancellation policy and how to cancel, describing the cancellation mechanism; for free gifts or trials, disclose how to cancel and allow cancellation before the consumer pays.

exposure.remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
requirements.title: Provide a cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism
requirements.summary: Provide a toll-free number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism, described in the acknowledgment.

exposure.remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
requirements.title: Online sign-ups must be able to cancel exclusively online
requirements.summary: A business that lets consumers accept online must allow termination exclusively online, which may include a termination email formatted and provided by the business that can be sent without additional information.

exposure.remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Tennessee automatic renewal of subscription services (Consumer Protection Act)
requirements.title: Notice of material changes with cancellation information
requirements.summary: For a material change in accepted terms, give a clear and conspicuous notice of the change and retainable information on how to cancel.

notice_window.description: any time before the price change

exposure.remedies: Refund on request within seven days (Pub. Ch. 835, 2024); private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Utah Automatic Renewal Contracts Act
requirements.title: Renewal notice 30-60 days ahead when the next paid term is longer than 45 days
requirements.summary: For a contract that automatically renews at the end of a definite paid term for a subsequent paid term longer than 45 days, send a notice 30 to 60 days before the renewal that clearly and conspicuously discloses the renewal date, the total renewal cost, and the options for cancelling.

exposure.remedies: Non-compliant renewal provisions are void; Division of Consumer Protection administrative fines and civil penalties up to $2,500 per violation.

requirements.law: Utah Automatic Renewal Contracts Act
requirements.title: Trial-ending notice at least 3 days before any trial period offer expires
requirements.summary: For a trial period offer (a period to sample a product or service without payment), send a notice at least 3 days before the trial expires that clearly and conspicuously discloses the expiration date, the price (and any further purchase obligations) after it, and the options for cancelling.

notice_window.description: at least 3 days before the trial ends

exposure.remedies: Non-compliant renewal provisions are void; Division of Consumer Protection administrative fines and civil penalties up to $2,500 per violation.

requirements.law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
requirements.title: Present the renewal terms clearly and conspicuously before the consumer is obligated, next to the consent request
requirements.summary: Before the consumer becomes obligated and before the initial order is completed, present the automatic renewal offer terms — continues until cancelled; the cancellation policy including how to find the cancellation mechanism; recurring charges and any change; each deadline (by date or frequency) to stop charges; the renewal term or that service is continuous; any minimum purchase obligation — clearly and conspicuously and in visual (or temporal) proximity to the request for consent.

exposure.remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

requirements.law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
requirements.title: Obtain affirmative consent before charging
requirements.summary: Before the initial order is completed, do not charge the consumer's card or third-party account without first obtaining affirmative consent to the agreement containing the offer terms.

exposure.remedies: Virginia Consumer Protection Act private suit (actual damages or $500, trebled to $1,500 if willful); a reported $5,000-per-violation figure after the 2026 amendments is unverified (open question 12). Small businesses count as consumers; the good-faith defense was removed in 2026.

requirements.title: Send a retainable acknowledgment; for free trials explain how to cancel before paying
requirements.summary: Provide a retainable acknowledgment with the offer terms, cancellation policy and how to cancel; if the offer includes a free trial, also disclose how to cancel the trial before the consumer pays or becomes obligated to pay.

requirements.law: Virginia Automatic Renewal Offers and Continuous Service Offers
requirements.title: Cancellation at least as easy as sign-up, through every sign-up channel, without a required agent
requirements.summary: Provide a cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism that is clear and conspicuous and easy to find; at least as easy as the sign-up mechanism; available through each method by which consumers can sign up (in-person sign-ups: online or by phone); no required interaction with a live or virtual agent unless sign-up is only possible through one; phone cancellation effectuated promptly on a number answered or recording messages during business hours, free of charge and no more costly than sign-up; print publications sold in person, by pamphlet or mail must be cancellable online or by phone.

requirements.title: Cancellation mechanism described in the acknowledgment (2018-2026 text)
requirements.summary: Provide a toll-free number, email address, postal address (only if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use cancellation mechanism, described in the acknowledgment.

requirements.title: Notice of material changes before implementation

requirements.law: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
requirements.title: State the automatic renewal terms clearly and conspicuously, in plain language and bold-face type
requirements.summary: The contract must state the terms of the automatic renewal provision clearly and conspicuously in plain, unambiguous language in bold-face type.

exposure.remedies: Vermont Consumer Protection Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
requirements.title: Separate affirmative opt-in to the automatic renewal
requirements.summary: In addition to accepting the contract, the consumer must take an affirmative action to opt in to the automatic renewal provision.

exposure.remedies: Vermont Consumer Protection Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
requirements.title: Renewal notice 30-60 days before the earliest of renewal, termination or cancellation deadline
requirements.summary: If the consumer opted in, send written or electronic notice 30 to 60 days before the earliest of the automatic renewal date, the termination date, or the date by which the consumer must give notice to cancel, stating the date the contract will terminate with a clear statement that it will renew automatically unless cancelled on or before that date, and the length and any additional terms of the renewal period.

exposure.remedies: Vermont Consumer Protection Act; private enforcement through the state's general consumer-protection (UDAP) statute is inferred, not verified.

requirements.law: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
requirements.title: Provide a cost-effective, timely, easy-to-use cancellation mechanism
requirements.summary: Provide a toll-free telephone number, email address, postal address (if billing directly) or another cost-effective, timely and easy-to-use mechanism for cancelling.

requirements.law: Vermont consumer contracts; automatic renewal
requirements.title: Online sign-ups must be able to cancel exclusively online
requirements.summary: If the consumer accepted the contract online, permit termination exclusively online, which may include a termination email formatted and provided by the seller that the consumer can send without additional information.

requirements.law: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act (ROSCA)
requirements.title: Terms must not deny the simple mechanism to stop recurring charges
requirements.summary: ROSCA requires simple mechanisms for consumers to stop recurring charges. Terms of service or policies that say a subscription cannot be canceled, or that it can only be canceled by phone, mail or in writing, contradict that mechanism and mislead subscribers about how to stop the charges.

exposure.remedies: ROSCA: FTC and state attorneys general only. Violations are treated as FTC rule violations: civil penalties up to $53,088 per violation (counted per consumer) and consumer redress (e.g. Amazon $2.5B, Adobe $150M).

requirements.law: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act (ROSCA)
requirements.title: Refund and cancellation terms must match what the offer promises
requirements.summary: All material terms of a negative-option offer must be disclosed clearly before billing information is collected. A refund or money-back promise made in marketing or at checkout that the written refund policy takes back ("no refunds", a shorter window) is a misrepresented material term.

exposure.remedies: ROSCA: FTC and state attorneys general only. Violations are treated as FTC rule violations: civil penalties up to $53,088 per violation (counted per consumer) and consumer redress (e.g. Amazon $2.5B, Adobe $150M).

requirements.law: California Automatic Renewal Law
requirements.title: Terms must allow online sign-ups to cancel online, at will and immediately
requirements.summary: Consumers who accepted an automatic renewal offer online must be able to terminate exclusively online, at will, and without steps that obstruct or delay immediate termination. Terms that require a phone call, a letter, written notice or a notice period before cancelling conflict with that right.

exposure.remedies: No private right in the ARL itself (Mayron v. Google, 2020): plaintiffs sue under the UCL, FAL and CLRA and must show economic injury; CLRA requires a 30-day demand letter before damages. Goods or services provided without the required consent are an unconditional gift (§ 17603); all civil remedies are available (§ 17604, with a good-faith-compliance safe harbor). Public enforcement by the district attorneys' task force (CART): penalties plus restitution (HelloFresh $7.5M). Typical class settlements $0.6M-$7.5M.

requirements.law: California Automatic Renewal Law
requirements.title: Terms of service restate the automatic renewal offer terms
requirements.summary: The automatic renewal offer terms (that the subscription continues until canceled, the cancellation policy, the recurring charges, the renewal term and how to cancel) must be presented clearly before the subscription is fulfilled. The Terms of service the consumer agrees to should state the same terms, so the contract does not silently differ from the checkout disclosure.
